title: The Camino Francés from Sarria to Santiago

bestPeriod.window: May to June and September to October
bestPeriod.note: July and August fill every albergue by early afternoon.
bestPeriod.avoid: November to March, short days and many albergues closed
bestPeriod.raw: May to June, September to October

food.note: Menú del peregrino €12 to €15, café breakfasts

transport.note: Bus from Santiago airport to Sarria and back to the airport

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, five walking days of 19 to 29 km on good paths, about 5 to 7 hours each

gatewayAirport: SCQ Santiago de Compostela, bus to Sarria via Lugo in about 2 h 30 min
summary: The last 100 km of the Camino Francés, the minimum that earns the Compostela. Five days on oak-lined lanes and stone villages from Sarria, through Portomarín on its reservoir, octopus in Melide and eucalyptus woods, to the Cathedral of Santiago and the pilgrims' Mass. Beds are €10 to €20 a night and dinner is a three-course menú for €13.
hook: 111 km in five days, beds from €10 a night, and the Compostela at the end.

itinerary.title: To Sarria
itinerary.morning: Fly to Santiago de Compostela, then the bus to Sarria via Lugo, about 2 h 30 min.
itinerary.afternoon: Get your credencial stamped at the parish church and check the first yellow arrow.
itinerary.evening: Pilgrim dinner on Rúa Maior and an early night.

itinerary.title: Sarria to Portomarín
itinerary.morning: Out through oak woods and hamlets; the **100 km stone** comes before lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to the Miño reservoir and the climb of stairs into Portomarín, rebuilt stone by stone above the water.
itinerary.evening: Tarta de Santiago and an evening walk on the church square.

itinerary.title: Portomarín to Palas de Rei
itinerary.morning: The longest climb of the week, up to Sierra Ligonde, about 720 m, on forest tracks.
itinerary.afternoon: Down through Ligonde and Eirexe to Palas de Rei.
itinerary.evening: Caldo gallego and a foot soak.

itinerary.title: Palas de Rei to Arzúa
itinerary.morning: The longest day, 29 km, on rolling lanes through Galician farms.
itinerary.afternoon: Pulpo a feira in Melide, octopus with paprika on wooden plates, the Camino's best lunch.
itinerary.evening: Cheese from Arzúa, famous for it, with bread and a beer.

photo.credit: Church of Santa María la Real del Sar
photo.author: Javier Pais

itinerary.title: Arzúa to O Pedrouzo
itinerary.morning: A shorter day under eucalyptus, with cafés every few kilometres.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in O Pedrouzo early and rest before the last stage.

itinerary.title: O Pedrouzo to Santiago
itinerary.morning: Up to Monte do Gozo, the Mount of Joy, for the first sight of the cathedral spires.
itinerary.afternoon: Into the old town and the Praza do Obradoiro; queue at the pilgrim office for the Compostela.
itinerary.evening: Celebration dinner on Rúa do Franco.

itinerary.title: Santiago, the Mass and home
itinerary.morning: The noon pilgrims' Mass in the Cathedral; the botafumeiro swings on feast days and some Fridays.
itinerary.afternoon: Rooftop tour of the cathedral, about €12, then the bus to the airport, 35 minutes.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming; signal is good in every village.
logistics.weather: Galicia is green because it rains; a light rain jacket every day, all year.
logistics.bookingWindows: Private albergues take bookings; public ones are first come from 13:00.
logistics.money: Small cafés are cash only; ATMs in every stage town.
logistics.transportRules: Luggage transfer between albergues costs about €5 a stage per bag.
logistics.permits: The credencial, the pilgrim passport, with two stamps a day from Sarria for the Compostela.
logistics.health: Treat hot spots on the first day; pharmacies in every stage town.
logistics.gettingThere: Fly to Santiago; buses to Sarria run via Lugo.

proTips: Collect two stamps a day from Sarria: the pilgrim office asks for them on the last 100 km.
Start at 07:30 to finish before the afternoon heat and the albergue queue.

raw.Who It Suits: First-time pilgrims and walkers who want a week with meaning

typeSpecific.surface: Paths and quiet lanes, about 90% unpaved
typeSpecific.technicalRating: Waymarked with yellow arrows and stone markers every 500 m
typeSpecific.bookingTimeline: Private albergues a few days ahead, a week in summer

whatCouldGoWrong: Summer albergues fill by early afternoon; book private beds or start early.
Blisters on day two end more Caminos than anything; stop and treat them early.
